name: North Ridge via Jaws' Tooth

waypoints.name: Elbow Lake Trail - North Trailhead (FR 38)
waypoints.note: Low-elevation trailhead off FR 38 via Mosquito Lake Rd; Northwest Forest Pass required, and FR 38 is gated Dec 1-Jun 15 at Wallace Creek. This is a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which sits at the trail's south end off Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12.
waypoints.directions: From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme and turn right (east) onto Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, crossing the Middle Fork Nooksack River, then continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the north trailhead for the Elbow Lake Trail at about 2,000 feet. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and FR 38 is gated at Wallace Creek from December 1 through June 15. Do not confuse this with the Pioneer Camp trailhead, which sits at the trail's south end off the Baker Lake Highway (FSR 12). As of mid-2026 FR 38 was damaged in the December 2025 floods with no published repair date, so confirm current road conditions with the Mount Baker Ranger District before you drive in.

waypoints.name: Middle Fork Nooksack River crossing
waypoints.note: No bridge on this side — the unofficial log crossing with rope handrails was destroyed in the December 2025 floods and has not been replaced, so this is a ford that can be unfordable at high flow.
waypoints.directions: Follow Elbow Lake Trail #697 about 0.2 mile from the trailhead to the Middle Fork Nooksack River. There is no bridge here, so it is a ford that can be impassable at high water.

waypoints.name: Green Creek climbers' path junction (Hildebrand Creek switchback)
waypoints.note: Unmaintained, sparsely blue-blazed climbers' trail for Green Creek Cirque splits off the maintained Elbow Lake Trail #697 at a switchback near Hildebrand Creek — easy to walk past, watch for paint blazes and flagging.
waypoints.directions: Beyond the river, continue on the Elbow Lake Trail as it climbs to a switchback near Hildebrand Creek, where the unmaintained, sparsely blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' path leaves the trail. It is easy to walk past, so watch for paint blazes and flagging.

waypoints.name: Green Creek at the cirque mouth
waypoints.note: Green Creek runs clear here at the entrance to the Green Creek Cirque — treat this as the last reliable water before the upper slabs and summit ridge.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path west up the Green Creek drainage to the mouth of the Green Creek Cirque, where the creek is the last reliable water before the upper slabs and ridge.

waypoints.name: Connecting ridge gain point south of South Twin
waypoints.note: Loose, engaging 3rd/4th-class scrambling out of the cirque gains the ridge crest just south of South Twin; from here the route turns south along the connecting ridge to Skookum on grippy olivine.
waypoints.directions: Scramble loose third- and fourth-class ground out of the cirque to gain the ridge crest just south of South Twin, where the rock turns to grippy olivine.

waypoints.name: Skookum Peak summit
waypoints.note: True summit (also known as 'Kloke Peak'); descend the loose south-west side by third-class gullies rather than reversing the ridge, then return to the Green Creek Cirque and the climbers' path.

overview: Skookum Peak is one of the summits of the Twin Sisters Range west of Mount Baker, a chain famous for its reddish-orange olivine (dunite) rock — a rare exposed fragment of the earth's mantle and the largest such body in the Western Hemisphere. The peak lies on the ridge system extending south from South Twin, the range highpoint, and is a highlight of the popular east-side Green Creek Circuit linkup with South Twin, Jaws' Tooth, Little Sister, and Cinderella. It is also known unofficially as 'Kloke Peak': in 2022 Washington's Committee on Geographic Names took up a proposal to formally rename it after Anacortes climber Dallas Kloke, who with Dave Dixon made the first recorded ascent in September 1972 and put up a dozen new routes across the Twin Sisters through the 1980s before his death in a 2010 North Cascades climbing accident. Both names are still used interchangeably by climbers (commonly written 'Skookum (Kloke)').

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme, turn right (east) on Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, and continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which is actually on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12).

approach: From the Mount Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on WA-9 to Acme, turn right (east) on Mosquito Lake Road for about 9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, and continue onto Forest Road 38 for roughly 11 miles to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from 'Pioneer Camp,' which is actually on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12). From there, follow Elbow Lake Trail #697 across the Middle Fork Nooksack and up to a switchback near Hildebrand Creek, then pick up the unmaintained Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque beneath Skookum's north/east flank before gaining the ridge. This whole approach is compromised: FSR 38 was damaged in the December 2025 floods and has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026, and the unofficial log crossing with rope handrails over the Middle Fork Nooksack near the trailhead was also washed out — confirm current conditions with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.

access.fees: $5 daily or $30 annual Northwest Forest Pass.
access.rules: Standard Forest Service dispersed-use/Leave No Trace rules apply for day use and backcountry camping.
access.permit: No day-use climbing permit required; standard Mount Baker Wilderness group-size/LNT rules apply.
access.closures: FSR 38, the primary access road, was significantly damaged in the December 2025 floods and has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026. The unofficial log crossing with rope handrails over the Middle Fork Nooksack at the Elbow Lake trailhead was also destroyed in the same storms and has not been replaced. Even in a normal year, FSR 38 has a seasonal gate at Wallace Creek, about 1.3 miles before the trailhead, closed roughly December 1 through June 15.
access.landManager: U.S. Forest Service — Mount Baker Ranger District, Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Sedro-Woolley, WA).
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass (or an America the Beautiful / National Parks pass) displayed at the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (FSR 38) — a separate trailhead from Pioneer Camp, which is on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12.

overnight_permit.where: Camping is on unregulated Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest land; no wilderness permit or registration is needed.

road.name: Forest Road 38 (via Mosquito Lake Road from Acme) to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from Pioneer Camp, which is on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12)
road.status: Damaged by December 2025 flooding and closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026 — confirm current status with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.
road.driveNote: From the Mount Baker Ranger District (Sedro-Woolley), take WA-9 north to Acme, turn right on Mosquito Lake Road for ~9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, then continue on FSR 38 for ~11 miles to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Normally gated at Wallace Creek (~1.3 miles before the trailhead) roughly December 1 through June 15, independent of flood damage.
